_comment_budget: 1800 train images / batch 16 = 112 steps per epoch. `total_epochs` overrides `total_steps`. val/recon is evaluated every epoch and the best model is written to checkpoint_best.pth.
_comment_fov: 64x64 CENTRE CROP, matching the NAMD benchmark. Every arm in nodule_quality_eval was built on patch[32:96, 32:96] -- byte-identical to a centre crop, and NOT to any downsample of the 128x128 patch (verified: no resize method matches, the crop matches exactly). resize_mode must be 'crop', not the default 'resize', or the model would see a different image than the benchmark.
_comment_label: NAMD-style light label supervision on the first stage, mirroring ldm/models/corrae.py:ContrastiveAutoencoderKL -- a single Linear over the FLATTENED SAMPLED latent to one logit, BCEWithLogitsLoss, added to the AE loss at weight 0.2 (their configs/autoencoder/contrastive-VAE.yaml value). The head lives OUTSIDE MultiHeadAEKL so the AE state dict stays loadable by the diffusion stage, which is how NAMD does it too: alignvae/predvae train the VAE with corrae, then load the weights into the plain AutoencoderKL for the LDM stage. NOT implemented: their companion contrastive feature_loss (KLDistanceLoss over the EHR vector, weight 1.0).
_comment_label_weight: NAMD uses 0.2, but that is calibrated to their LPIPS+NLL objective (order 0.1-1). Ours is plain MSE on [0,1] images (order 1e-3), where 0.2 made the label term 22x the TOTAL of every other loss and 228x the recon term -- the AE became a classifier that incidentally reconstructed, roughly doubling val recon error. 1e-3 puts the label term at ~11% of the other losses: a light auxiliary nudge at the same RELATIVE strength NAMD intended.
